title: Add mixed-workload benchmark scenarios to benchmark-lab + automated p95/throughput reporting
creator: Talia Benson
project: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype (Serving Runtime Performance: Kernel + Scheduling)
content:
Context / Why
Mixed prompt-length distributions (short chat prompts interleaved with long-context prompts) cause tail latency amplification via head-of-line blocking in continuous batching + KV-cache heavy decode. Scheduler prototype work needs a repeatable, standardized benchmark suite that:
- Reproduces the problem deterministically
- Produces comparable metrics across runtime builds/SKUs
- Generates an automated report suitable for perf-canary + release gates

Scope of this ticket
1) Add standardized mixed-workload scenarios to benchmark-lab (workload definitions + runner wiring)
2) Automate reporting: p50/p95/p99, TTFT, throughput, queue time, per-class (short/long) splits where available
3) Define comparison baselines and pass/fail thresholds for regressions (p95 + throughput) to support runtime-1.18 candidate evaluation

Non-goals
- Replacing the existing steady-state homogeneous decode benchmarks (keep those intact)
- Full admission-control testing (only minimal coupling)

Proposed scenarios (v1)
We’re adding 3 canonical mixes that map to what we see in anonymized traces and what SRE wants for canary guardrails:
A) 80/20 Short/Long ("chat-heavy")
- Short prompts: p50 ~ 128–256 tokens prompt, generate 128 tokens
- Long prompts: 4k–8k prompt, generate 128 tokens
- Goal: reduce user-visible p95 for shorts without materially regressing throughput

B) 50/50 Short/Long ("balanced")
- Stress fairness and aging/starvation prevention
- Goal: ensure long requests still make progress and p95 does not blow up

C) Long-spike ("burst long context")
- 2–5 minute window where long prompts jump to 60–70% of arrivals
- Goal: verify scheduler doesn’t destabilize kernel selection / batch formation and that rollback triggers are meaningful

Workload generation details
- Arrival process: Poisson arrivals with configurable target QPS; support fixed-seed mode for determinism
- Prompt corpus:
  - Synthetic prompts allowed for CI speed (token-count targeted, minimal text)
  - Optional replay mode for curated anonymized templates maintained by Claire (Drive link in benchmark plan)
- Runtime API: use existing benchmark-lab driver; add fields to capture TTFT (time-to-first-token) and queue time if runtime exposes them

Metrics captured (per run)
Required:
- End-to-end latency: p50/p95/p99
- TTFT: p50/p95
- Throughput: tokens/sec (total + by class where available)
- Queue time: p50/p95 (time waiting before dispatch)
- Error rate / timeouts

Nice-to-have (gated on runtime metrics availability):
- Prefill latency vs decode latency split
- Scheduler class metrics: dispatch share, starvation counters

Reporting format
- JSON summary artifact per scenario with:
  - runtime build identifier + git SHA
  - model, precision/quant profile, max batch tokens
  - hardware SKU + driver versions
  - scenario definition (mix, target QPS, warmup, duration)
  - metric table (overall + short/long)
- Human-readable markdown report generated from the JSON for CI links (posted as a build artifact)
- Comparison mode: baseline vs candidate diff table with deltas highlighted

Baseline / Comparison rules
Baselines are pinned to a known-good runtime build per model+SKU combo.
- Baseline source: latest stable runtime-1.17.x build that is currently serving in the region/pool used for perf-canary (Sahana to confirm exact tag)
- Baseline refresh policy: only update baseline after explicit approval from Runtime TL (Lena) + SRE sponsor (Sean) to avoid hiding regressions

Pass/fail thresholds (initial; can be tuned after we see noise)
- p95 latency (overall): must not regress by > +7% vs baseline in any scenario
- p95 latency (short class): should improve by >= -15% in 80/20 and >= -10% in 50/50 for the scheduler-prototype-on build; otherwise flag as “no win” (not a hard fail, but a release decision input)
- Throughput (tokens/sec): must not regress by > -3% overall
- Error rate: must not increase by > +0.2% absolute

Warmup + run protocol
- Warmup: 2 minutes to stabilize caches
- Measurement window: 10 minutes for 80/20 and 50/50; 15 minutes for long-spike
- Repeat runs: 3 iterations per scenario; report median and variance
- Fixed seed enabled for CI; allow non-fixed seed for exploratory runs

Implementation plan (benchmark-lab)
- Add scenario config definitions under mixed_workload/ (naming: mixed_80_20, mixed_50_50, mixed_long_spike)
- Extend runner to:
  - emit per-request class label (short/long) if provided by runtime response headers/trace tags; otherwise infer by prompt length used
  - collect TTFT + queue time from trace spans when available (fallback: client-side approximation if not)
- Add a report generator:
  - render summary tables
  - print “gate results” line for CI parsing

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Mixed-workload scenarios are runnable locally and in CI on at least one representative SKU
- [x] Report artifact includes p95/throughput deltas vs baseline with clear pass/fail signals
- [x] Scenario definitions are documented and reviewed by Runtime TL (Lena) + Benchmark methodology (Claire)
- [x] Outputs are consumable by perf-canary follow-up (ENG-2456)

Links
- Confluence benchmark plan: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/mixed-workload-benchmark-plan.json
- Initiative: sources/linear/engineering/ENG-2417-mixed-workload-scheduler-prototype-initiative.json
- Related PRs:
  - benchmark-lab: sources/github/benchmark-lab/pr-903-add-mixed-workload-scenarios.json
  - perf-canary follow-up: sources/github/perf-canary/pr-611-runtime-scheduler-canary-job.json

Status updates / comments (chronological)
2025-12-11 (Talia Benson)
- Created ticket. Aligning with Phase 2 deliverable: benchmark suite + automated reporting. Rina owns implementation, Claire to sanity-check workload protocol, Lena to approve thresholds.

2025-12-13 (Rina Kobayashi)
- Drafted scenario configs for 80/20 + 50/50. Long-spike needs clarity on exact ramp shape (step vs linear). Proposed: step change at t=5m for 3m, then return.

2025-12-16 (Claire Dubois)
- Please ensure runs are long enough to capture tail; 5m windows were too noisy in earlier trace replays. +1 on 10m measurement window. Also: keep synthetic prompts for CI but allow replay mode for "realistic" prompts in manual runs.

2025-12-18 (Lena Fischer)
- Threshold suggestion: don’t hard-fail on short p95 improvement (that becomes a decision input), but do hard-fail on overall p95 regression and throughput regression. Also ensure we record variance across repeats.

2025-12-20 (Rina Kobayashi)
- Implemented JSON summary output + markdown renderer. Added fixed-seed mode. Still missing queue time (needs runtime trace integration; likely lands with ENG-2441 metrics plumbing).

2026-01-06 (Rina Kobayashi)
- Open question: class labels. If runtime emits scheduler_class=short|long tag, we’ll consume it; otherwise we label by prompt_length threshold used by scenario generator.

2026-01-10 (Allison Grant)
- For perf-canary, ensure the JSON includes build ID + SKU + region; we want to correlate with Grafana dashboards. Also include timeouts separately from non-200 errors.

2026-01-14 (Rina Kobayashi)
- PR opened in benchmark-lab with scenarios + report generation. Added error breakdown fields and run metadata block.

2026-01-18 (Sean Gallagher)
- Baseline refresh policy looks good. Please document it in the repo README near “How to interpret gates.” SRE will treat baseline bumps as change-managed.

2026-01-24 (Rina Kobayashi)
- PR merged. Added README note about baseline bump approvals. Marking ticket Done. Next step: wire into perf-canary job (ENG-2456) and confirm baseline tag for runtime-1.17.x per SKU.

Notes / Follow-ups
- Queue time + prefill/decode split will improve once runtime exports trace spans consistently for both paths (tracked in ENG-2441).
- After first week of nightly runs, revisit thresholds based on observed noise and variance; likely tighten throughput gate if stable.
